gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-taviraj: Heavy tubing up top, a quieter hand below. Aaargh is at its best being commanding, every stem cut from one gauge, while Taviraj is at its best being bookish, with a restrained step between stem and joining stroke.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-trirong: Trirong reads like a dip pen used gently, its flared curve ends staying politely apart. And Aaargh, with its thickness holding steady round every curve, supplies the strong, commanding voice up front.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-trocchi: Trocchi draws its c as a wide ring, a dignified foil to the commanding, round-pen letters of Aaargh. Its bowls thin gently, so paragraphs would flow without any harsh jolts.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-uchen: Solid round bowls, then a gentler hand. Aaargh keeps its bowl walls uniform all the way round, while Uchen adds a dignified, understated stroke contrast and curves that welcome the eye.
gen-dafont-aaargh-ibm-plex-serif: IBM Plex Serif brings a quiet, authoritative contrast. Aaargh holds a constant stroke from top to baseline, while the slimmer horizontals and unclenched c here keep extended reading steady.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-amulya: Amulya keeps its curves generously open and its lowercase moderate, a contemporary foil to the tall, otherworldly Alien Encounters. Long stretches of it read smoothly, with no strain on the eye.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-chillax: Chillax runs a spaghetti-like monoline with pen-lifted curves left unfinished, loose and relaxed against the tall, otherworldly Alien Encounters. Its lowercase stays moderate where the heading's climbs much higher.
gen-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-spline-sa: Otherworldly spacing defines Alien Encounters, with big gaps between letter pairs and a high x-height. But Spline Sans stays approachable, its wire-bent curves and identical stroke weights settling things down.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-fanwood-text: Fanwood Text reads literary and bookish, its large-eyed lowercase swelling gently on the curves. Fanwood Text sits quietly beside Amadeus, whose bold, wide-stretched words hold a single weight throughout.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Wide-stretched words define Amadeus, each glyph drawn with an unmodulated line. And Noto Naskh Arabic, refined and very tall in the x-height, adds a lightly engraved modulation that feels like a quiet reply.
